title: AND, OR and IN
intro: Combining conditions. SQL handles AND before OR, so mixing them without parentheses changes the meaning. IN is the safe way to say "any of these values".

drills.title: Phone or chat, still open
drills.prompt: List tickets that came in by phone or chat and are still open.
rules: Open means status is 'open'.

drills.title: High stakes, waiting on the customer
drills.prompt: List high or urgent priority tickets that are pending.
rules: Priority is 'high' or 'urgent'.
Status is 'pending'.

drills.title: Two lists at once
drills.prompt: List tickets that still need work and came in through email or the web form.
rules: Still needs work means status is 'open' or 'pending'.
The web form channel is 'web'.

drills.title: Everything except
drills.prompt: List low priority tickets that aren't finished yet.
rules: Finished means status is 'solved' or 'closed'.
Priority is 'low'.

title: Writing dates
intro: Dates go in quotes with DATE in front, like DATE '2026-10-01'. A timestamp also has a time of day, which matters at the edges of a date range.

drills.title: The last day of September
drills.prompt: List every ticket created on September 30, 2026, at any time that day.
rules: created_at includes the time of day.

drills.title: Who left before August
drills.prompt: Which agents left before August 1, 2026?
rules: An agent left on the date in deactivated_at.

drills.title: Days to solve
drills.prompt: For urgent tickets created in September 2026 that have been solved, how many whole days did each take?
rules: A ticket has been solved if solved_at is filled in.
Name the column days_to_solve.

drills.title: The outage week
drills.prompt: List tickets created from July 9 through July 15, 2026, including both days.
rules: Include all of July 15, up to midnight.

title: Cleaning text
intro: Text typed by people needs cleaning before you compare or count it. Put functions inside each other: the innermost one runs first.

drills.title: Find the trials
drills.prompt: List helpdesk orgs that are trials: the word 'trial' appears somewhere in the name, in any capitalization.
rules: Match 'trial', 'Trial' or 'TRIAL'.

drills.title: Two functions, one value
drills.prompt: List each distinct category after making it lowercase and trimming spaces. Leave '-issue' alone for now.
rules: Name the column clean.

drills.title: August's top topics
drills.prompt: What were the three most common ticket topics in August 2026, after cleaning the categories?
rules: Clean a category by making it lowercase, removing a trailing '-issue', and trimming spaces.
Leave out tickets with no category after cleaning.
Most tickets first. If two topics tie, put them in alphabetical order.

drills.title: Tickets with no topic
drills.prompt: How many tickets have no category: missing, empty, or only spaces?
rules: Return one number, named no_category.

title: Joining tables
intro: ON says which rows belong together, so it uses =. A regular JOIN keeps only matches; a LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the first table and fills the other side with NULL when nothing matches.

drills.title: Who has the urgent queue
drills.prompt: List open urgent tickets with the name of the agent assigned to each.
rules: Open means status is 'open'.

drills.title: Churned customers in the helpdesk
drills.prompt: List customers the CRM marks as churned, with the name of their helpdesk org.
rules: Churned means the CRM status is 'churned'.

drills.title: Enterprise in the CRM
drills.prompt: List helpdesk orgs whose customer is on the enterprise plan in the CRM, with that plan.
rules: Use the CRM's plan_tier, not the helpdesk.

drills.title: Tickets from unknown customers
drills.prompt: List tickets whose helpdesk org can't be matched to a CRM customer.
rules: An org is unmatched if its crm_customer_id is blank or doesn't match any customer_id.

title: Counting by group
intro: GROUP BY puts rows with the same value together, and COUNT, MIN or MAX work inside each group. Every column in SELECT is either grouped or wrapped in one of those.

drills.title: Tickets per channel
drills.prompt: How many tickets came in through each channel, across all six months?
rules: Name the count tickets.

drills.title: Tickets per team
drills.prompt: How many tickets has each support team been assigned?
rules: A ticket belongs to the team of the agent it's assigned to.
Name the count tickets.

drills.title: Oldest in each lane
drills.prompt: For tickets that still need work, how many are there at each priority, and when was the oldest one created?
rules: A ticket still needs work if its status is open or pending.
Name the columns tickets and oldest.

title: Filtering groups
intro: WHERE filters rows before they're grouped. HAVING filters the groups afterward, so it can use counts and other totals.

drills.title: Busy orgs in September
drills.prompt: Which orgs filed more than 10 tickets in September 2026?
rules: Name the count tickets.

drills.title: High stakes queues
drills.prompt: Which agents have at least 5 high or urgent tickets that still need work?
rules: A ticket still needs work if its status is open or pending.
Name the count tickets.

drills.title: Heavy days
drills.prompt: Which days in September 2026 had more than 40 tickets?
rules: Group by calendar day, not by the exact time.
Name the columns day and tickets.

title: Labeling with CASE
intro: CASE WHEN checks conditions in order and returns the label of the first one that's true, or the ELSE label. It's how you turn values into categories, or count only some rows.

drills.title: Fast lane
drills.prompt: Label each ticket that still needs work as 'fast lane' if it's high or urgent priority, otherwise 'standard'.
rules: A ticket still needs work if its status is open or pending.
Name the label lane.

drills.title: Weekend tickets
drills.prompt: How many tickets were created on weekends versus weekdays?
rules: In DuckDB, dayofweek(created_at) gives 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday.
Label rows 'weekend' or 'weekday', and name the columns day_type and tickets.

drills.title: Counting only some rows
drills.prompt: For each channel, show the total number of tickets and how many of them were urgent.
rules: Name the columns tickets and urgent_tickets.

title: Grouping by time
intro: date_trunc rounds a timestamp down to the start of its week, month or year, so all the rows in that period share one value you can group by.

drills.title: Weeks of September
drills.prompt: How many tickets were created in each week that started in September 2026?
rules: Weeks start on Monday; show each week as its first day.
Include a week if its Monday is in September, even if it ends in October.
Name the columns week and tickets.

drills.title: Urgent by month
drills.prompt: How many urgent tickets came in each month?
rules: Show each month as its first day.
Name the columns month and urgent_tickets.

drills.title: Month and channel
drills.prompt: How many tickets came in each month through each channel?
rules: Show each month as its first day.
Name the count tickets.

title: Building in steps
intro: A CTE names a step: WITH step_name AS (a query), then the main query reads from step_name like a table. Big questions get easier when you answer them in small named steps.

drills.title: Orgs over 15
drills.prompt: How many orgs filed more than 15 tickets from July through September 2026?
rules: Step 1: count tickets per org in that period. Step 2: count the orgs over 15.
Return one number, named orgs.

drills.title: The average org
drills.prompt: On average, how many tickets did an org file in September 2026?
rules: Average over orgs that filed at least one ticket in September.
Round to one decimal place and name it avg_tickets.

drills.title: Above their team's average
drills.prompt: Which active agents have more tickets still needing work than the average active agent on their own team?
rules: A ticket still needs work if its status is open or pending.
Active means deactivated_at is empty.
Compare each agent with their own team's average, not everyone's.
Name the count open_tickets.
